newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen plans to issue one-month T-bills weekly.
newsitem.headline: Yemen plans to issue one-month T-bills weekly.

text.p: Yemen plans to issue treasury bills weekly instead of monthly, a Central Bank official said.
The Bank plans "to offer the special treasury bills weekly and not monthly...but the maturities will continue to be monthly," the official said without giving a starting date.

The plan would "benefit the government in financing emergencies in government spending...as it is known that the central bank covers the deficit in the government's budget from treasury bill revenues".
The deficit for 1996 is projected at 25.5 billion rials.
Yemen currently issues 91- and 182-day bills every month.
The official said the Bank also planned "to issue treasury bills to the bearer rather than to individual names...in the next few weeks".
Yemen first introduced treasury bills last December.
